ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the input signal ui of the operational amplifier is connected through resistor R1 to the inverting input terminal (the terminal marked −); the output terminal u0 is fed back through the feedback resistor RF to the same inverting input node; the non-inverting input terminal (the terminal marked +) is grounded through resistor R. Therefore this circuit is the standard inverting proportional amplifier circuit of an ideal operational amplifier. Reasoning: The closed-loop voltage gain of an inverting amplifier is AUF = u0/ui = -RF/R1. Given R1 = 1 kΩ, RF = 10 kΩ, so AUF = -10 kΩ / 1 kΩ = -10. According to the problem requirement to keep one decimal place, the result is -10.0.

method.method_draft: First note from the image that the plus input is grounded through R, so for an ideal op amp v+ = 0 and v- = 0 by virtual short. Since no current enters the op-amp input, KCL at the inverting node gives (ui - 0)/R1 + (u0 - 0)/RF = 0, so u0/ui = -RF/R1. Insert the text values R1 = 1 kΩ and RF = 10 kΩ to get AUF = -10, or -10.0 to one decimal place.

图像描述：附图显示一个理想运算放大器比例放大电路。输入电压 ui 通过电阻 R1 接到运放的反相输入端（标有 “−”）；输出端 u0 通过反馈电阻 RF 返回到同一个反相输入节点；同相输入端（标有 “+”）通过电阻 R 接地。因此这是反相比例运算放大器结构。
